notes: Background: Pivotlane builds a conversational layer on top of ticketing + internal tools; primary metric = end-to-end agent latency and correct tool invocations.
Initial ask: Start on Hosted API for speed of integration, demonstrable streaming SLOs, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and data controls.
Latency SLOs: first-byte streaming target 150-200ms regionally; token-generation tail SLO 300ms average for new messages (goal).
POC scope: 3-week proof-of-concept — 2 regions (us-east/us-west), tool calling to internal CRM (secure lambda), compare responses across model variants.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market procurement — wants clear ARR math if switching to Dedicated. Asked for quantized model recommendations in Optimize to save GPU cycles.
Prompt/eval gating: Needs automated regression detection on prompt sets (regressions in expected tool call structure or hallucination rate). Wants webhook to block canary rollout if eval fails.
A/B + canary: requested example configs for 10% canary -> 30% -> 100% rollout with automatic rollback on quality drop. Wants built-in prompt set evaluation between rollouts.
SE notes: They ran token latency vs. model-size tests. Hosted was fast but noisy at peak; Dedicated promised stable p95 latency. Asking for queue/batching knobs to trade throughput vs. latency.
Quote from CTO in demo: "If we can't guarantee sub-200ms first byte on common queries, adoption inside our product will stall."
Security ask: SSO/SAML for admin console, customer-managed KMS for key material, audit logs for every model call (token-level redaction options desirable).
Integration: Tool calling path must support signed short-lived tokens and idempotent calls; demo showed successful mapping to internal CRM createTicket API (no PII persisted).

POC results summary: Hosted API baseline – median first-byte 120ms, p95 340ms during bursts. After SE tuning (smaller batch windows + caching), p95 down to ~220ms. Dedicated sims project p95 <200ms with reserved GPUs.
Open questions from Pivotlane: clear SLA for streaming latency, pricing for sustained burst capacity, contract terms for Dedicated commit, and regen gating latency impact.
Next technical ask: Run 48-hour soak with realistic traffic and our eval harness (prompt sets + scoring) to validate automatic rollback triggers on regressions.
Procurement: CFO wants two-sided pricing scenarios (hosted pay-as-you-go vs. 12mo Dedicated commit) and estimated savings from Optimize suggestions.
Short-term blockers: internal security questionnaire outstanding, waiting on dedicated capacity quota confirmation from infra team.
